question: Air brakes are actually made up of how many different braking systems?
choice_a: Two: service and parking
choice_b: Four: service, parking, emergency, and auxiliary
choice_c: One combined system
choice_d: Three: service, parking, and emergency
explanation: The manual states air brakes are really three different braking systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 5, Introduction

question: Which braking system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving?
choice_a: The spring brake system
choice_c: The service brake system
choice_d: The emergency brake system
explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 5, Introduction

question: If the air compressor has its own oil supply, what should you check before driving?
choice_a: The transmission fluid level
choice_c: The coolant temperature
choice_d: The oil level of the compressor
explanation: If the compressor has its own oil supply, you should check the oil level before driving.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.1, Air Compressor

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor stop the compressor from pumping air (the "cut-out" level)?
choice_a: 150 psi
choice_c: 125 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: When air tank pressure rises to the cut-out level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.2, Air Compressor Governor

question: What is the purpose of the air storage tanks (reservoirs)?
choice_a: To store excess engine coolant
choice_b: To filter oil out of the fuel system
choice_c: To cool the compressed air before it reaches the brake chambers
choice_d: To hold compressed air so the brakes can be used several times, even if the compressor stops working
explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air and will hold enough air to allow the brakes to be used several times, even if the compressor stops working.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.3, Air Storage Tanks

question: With a manually operated drain valve, when must you drain the air tanks yourself?
choice_a: Only when the low air warning comes on
choice_c: At the end of each day of driving
choice_d: Only once a week
explanation: Manually operated drain valves must be drained by the driver at the end of each day of driving.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.4, Air Tank Drains

question: What is the purpose of an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system?
choice_a: To reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather
choice_c: To increase brake pad friction
choice_d: To clean the brake drums
explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator to put alcohol into the air system, which helps reduce the risk of ice in air brake valves and other parts during cold weather.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.5, Alcohol Evaporator

question: Where is the safety relief valve installed, and at what pressure does it usually open?
choice_a: In the parking brake control, at 125 psi
choice_b: In the last tank before the brake chambers, at 100 psi
choice_c: In the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, usually set to open at 150 psi
choice_d: In the brake pedal linkage, at 55 psi
explanation: A safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, and it is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.6, Safety Valve

question: What is another name for the brake pedal on an air brake system?
choice_a: The slack adjuster
choice_b: The foot valve or treadle valve
choice_c: The relay valve
choice_d: The governor valve
explanation: The brake pedal is also called the foot valve or treadle valve.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.7, The Brake Pedal

question: What is the most common type of foundation brake used at each wheel?
choice_a: The s-cam drum brake
choice_c: The disc brake
choice_d: The spring brake
explanation: Foundation brakes are used at each wheel, and the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.8, Foundation Brakes

question: In an s-cam brake, what happens when you push the brake pedal?
choice_a: A wedge is pulled out from between the brake shoes
choice_b: Air is let into each brake chamber, pushing a rod that turns the s-cam and forces the brake shoes against the drum
choice_c: The power screw releases the caliper
choice_d: Hydraulic fluid directly clamps the drum
explanation: Air is let into each brake chamber, air pressure pushes the rod out and turns the s-cam, which forces the brake shoes apart and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.8, S-cam Brakes

question: In a wedge brake, what does the brake chamber push rod push?
choice_a: A wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum
choice_b: An s-cam that twists the camshaft
choice_c: A caliper directly against the tire
choice_d: A power screw that clamps a rotor
explanation: In wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.8, Wedge Brakes

question: What does the supply pressure gauge tell you?
choice_a: How hard you are pressing the brake pedal
choice_c: The temperature of the brake drums
choice_d: How much pressure is in the air tanks
explanation: All vehicles with air brakes have a pressure gauge connected to the air tank that tells you how much pressure is in the air tanks.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.9, Supply Pressure Gauges

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 75 psi
explanation: A warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 55 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.11, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is the "wig wag" warning device?
choice_a: A mechanical arm that drops into your view when pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_c: A dashboard light that flashes red and blue
choice_d: A gauge needle that turns yellow
explanation: The wig wag device drops a mechanical arm into your view when the pressure in the system drops below 55 psi.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.11, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: How does the air brake system warn drivers behind you when you apply the brakes?
choice_a: With a mechanical flag on the rear bumper
choice_c: With a horn that sounds automatically
choice_d: With an electric switch that works by air pressure and turns on the brake lights
explanation: The air brake system uses an electric switch that works by air pressure to turn on the brake lights when you put on the air brakes.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.12, Stop Light Switch

question: What did front brake limiting valves on older vehicles (made before 1975) do in the "slippery" position?
choice_a: They shut off the rear brakes entirely
choice_c: They increased front brake pressure by half
choice_d: They cut the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half
explanation: When the control is put in the slippery position, the limiting valve cuts the normal air pressure to the front brakes by half.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.13, Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why must trucks, truck tractors, and buses be equipped with emergency and parking brakes held on by mechanical force?
choice_a: Because air pressure can eventually leak away
choice_b: Because mechanical force is cheaper to produce
choice_c: Because it is required only for buses
choice_d: Because mechanical brakes stop faster
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.14, Spring Brakes

question: At what pressure range will tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on?
choice_a: 125 to 150 psi
choice_c: 55 to 80 psi
choice_d: 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi)
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi).
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.14, Spring Brakes

question: In newer vehicles with air brakes, what does the diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob do?
choice_a: It controls the alcohol evaporator only
choice_b: It only operates the low pressure warning buzzer
choice_c: You push it in to apply the parking brakes and pull it out to release them
choice_d: You pull it out to apply the parking brakes (spring brakes) and push it in to release them
explanation: You pull the diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull knob out to put the parking brakes (spring brakes) on, and push it in to release them.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.15, Parking Brake Controls

question: What does ABS do?
choice_a: It shortens stopping distance in all conditions
choice_b: It replaces the need for a parking brake
choice_c: It is a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_d: It automatically increases your following distance
explanation: ABS is a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.16, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps on vehicles equipped with ABS?
choice_a: Red
choice_c: Yellow
choice_d: Green
explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to tell you if something isn't working.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.1.16, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What is a dual air brake system?
choice_a: A system with two safety valves but one set of tanks
choice_b: A single brake system with two compressors
choice_c: Two separate air brake systems, each with its own air tanks, hoses, and lines, which use a single set of brake controls
choice_d: A system that uses hydraulic fluid as a backup to air
explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems, which use a single set of brake controls; each system has its own air tanks, hoses, lines, etc.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 5.2, Dual Air Brake

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, what minimum pressure should you allow the compressor to build up in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 100 psi
choice_c: 125 psi
choice_d: 85 psi
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Section 5.2, Dual Air Brake

question: When checking slack adjusters on s-cam brakes, if a slack adjuster moves more than about how far where the push rod attaches, it probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: One inch
choice_c: One quarter inch
choice_d: Six inches
explanation: If a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.2, Check Slack Adjusters on S-cam Brakes

question: What is the most common problem found in roadside inspections related to brakes?
choice_a: Out-of-adjustment brakes
choice_c: Cracked brake drums
choice_d: Missing safety valves
explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes are the most common problem found in roadside inspections, and vehicles with too much brake slack can be very hard to stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.2, Check Slack Adjusters on S-cam Brakes

topic: Inspecting Air Brakes - Drums, Linings, Hoses
question: What is the limit on cracks in brake drums (or discs)?
choice_a: Cracks up to the full width of the friction area are acceptable
choice_b: Cracks are acceptable as long as they are not visible from outside
choice_c: Any crack requires immediate replacement regardless of length
choice_d: They must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area
explanation: Brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.2, Check Brake Drums (or Discs), Linings, and Hoses

question: During the final air brake check, at approximately what pressure should the air compressor start pumping, and at what pressure should the governor cut it out?
choice_a: Start at about 100 psi, cut-out at about 125 psi
choice_b: Start at about 55 psi, cut-out at about 100 psi
choice_c: Start at about 125 psi, cut-out at about 150 psi
choice_d: Start at about 20 psi, cut-out at about 45 psi
explanation: Pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi and stop (cut-out) at about 125 psi, checking manufacturer's specifications.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Check Air Compressor Governor Cut-in and Cut-out Pressures

question: With a fully-charged air system (typically 125 psi), engine off and parking brake released, what is the maximum allowable air loss rate for a single vehicle?
choice_a: Less than one psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than five psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than three psi in one minute
explanation: The loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Test Air Leakage Rate

question: With a fully-charged air system, engine off and parking brake released, what is the maximum allowable air loss rate for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Less than four psi in one minute
choice_b: Less than two psi in one minute
choice_c: Less than three psi in one minute
choice_d: Less than five psi in one minute
explanation: The loss rate should be less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Test Air Leakage Rate

question: During the low pressure warning signal test, before what tank pressure must the warning signal come on?
choice_a: Before pressure drops to less than 100 psi
choice_b: Before pressure drops to less than 55 psi
choice_c: Before pressure drops to less than 20 psi
choice_d: Before pressure drops to less than 125 psi
explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops to less than 55 psi in the air tank (or the tank with the lowest air pressure, in dual air systems).
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Test Low Pressure Warning Signal

question: During the check that spring brakes come on automatically, at approximately what pressure range should the parking brake valve close (pop out) on a single vehicle?
choice_a: 0 to 10 psi
choice_c: 55 to 80 psi
choice_d: 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The parking brake valve should close (pop out) when the air pressure falls to the manufacturer's specification, which is 20 to 45 psi, causing the spring brakes to come on.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Check That Spring Brakes Come On Automatically

topic: Rate of Air Pressure Buildup Test
question: In dual air systems, at operating rpms, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
choice_a: 45 seconds
choice_c: 30 seconds
choice_d: 15 seconds
explanation: When the engine is at operating rpms, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Check Rate of Air Pressure Buildup

topic: Rate of Air Pressure Buildup Test
question: In single air systems (pre-1975), typical requirements are pressure build-up from 50 to 90 psi within how long, with the engine idling at 600-900 rpm?
choice_a: 3 minutes
choice_c: 5 minutes
choice_d: 1 minute
explanation: In single air systems (pre-1975), typical requirements are pressure build-up from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes with the engine at an idle speed of 600-900 rpms.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Check Rate of Air Pressure Buildup

question: How do you test the parking brake during the final air brake check?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake while the vehicle is still moving forward at 20 mph
choice_b: Stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that it will hold
choice_c: Drive at highway speed and apply the parking brake suddenly
choice_d: Check only the dashboard indicator light
explanation: To test the parking brake, stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.3.3, Test Parking Brake

question: For a normal stop with air brakes, what should you control?
choice_a: The parking brake knob
choice_c: The pressure on the brake pedal so the vehicle comes to a smooth, safe stop
choice_d: The alcohol evaporator level
explanation: For normal stops, push the brake pedal down and control the pressure so the vehicle comes to a smooth, safe stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.1, Normal Stops

question: What happens to a vehicle without ABS when you brake hard on slippery surfaces and the wheels lock up?
choice_a: The vehicle automatically corrects itself
choice_c: You may lose steering control, skid, jackknife, or even spin the vehicle
choice_d: The spring brakes automatically engage to compensate
explanation: When your steering wheels lock up, you lose steering control; when your other wheels lock up, you may skid, jackknife, or even spin the vehicle.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.2, Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: How does ABS help a driver during hard braking?
choice_a: It disables the parking brake to prevent skidding
choice_b: It automatically steers the vehicle around obstacles
choice_c: It increases braking force beyond normal levels
choice_d: It senses impending lockup, reduces braking pressure to a safe level, and helps you maintain control
explanation: The ABS computer senses impending lockup, reduces the braking pressure to a safe level, and you maintain control.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.2, Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: What are the two methods described for making an emergency stop while keeping the vehicle in a straight line?
choice_a: Engine braking and pumping the brakes
choice_c: Parking brake and hand valve braking
choice_d: Controlled braking and stab braking
explanation: You can use the controlled braking method or the stab braking method to keep your vehicle in a straight line during an emergency stop.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.3, Emergency Stops

question: In controlled braking, what should you do if the wheels lock or you need a large steering adjustment?
choice_a: Shift into neutral immediately
choice_c: Continue applying maximum brake pressure
choice_d: Release the brakes, then re-apply the brakes as soon as you can
explanation: With controlled braking, if you need to make a larger steering adjustment or if the wheels lock, release the brakes and re-apply them as soon as you can.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.3, Emergency Stops

question: About how many additional feet does the air brake lag distance add at 55 mph on dry pavement?
choice_a: About 10 feet
choice_c: About 32 feet
choice_d: About 100 feet
explanation: The air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.4, Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, what is the approximate total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Over 600 feet
choice_c: Over 200 feet
choice_d: Over 450 feet
explanation: At 55 mph for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance is over 450 feet.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.4, Stopping Distance

question: What causes brake fade from excessive use of the service brakes?
choice_a: Water contamination in the brake lines
choice_c: Cold temperatures reduce brake shoe flexibility
choice_d: Excessive heat causes chemical changes in the brake lining, reducing friction, and causes drum expansion
explanation: Excessive use of the service brakes results in overheating and brake fade; the excessive heat causes chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction and causes expansion of the brake drums.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.5, Brake Fading or Failure

question: On a long or steep downgrade, what is the proper role of the brakes relative to the engine braking effect?
choice_a: The brakes should be used exclusively, ignoring engine braking
choice_b: The parking brake should be applied continuously
choice_c: The use of brakes is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine, once in the proper low gear
choice_d: Brakes should never be used on a downgrade
explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine, once the vehicle is in the proper low gear.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.6, Proper Braking Technique

question: In the proper braking technique for downgrades, once your speed drops to about five mph below your "safe" speed, what should you do, and about how long should the brake application last?
choice_a: Shift to neutral; coast for one minute
choice_b: Pull the parking brake; hold for thirty seconds
choice_c: Release the brakes; the application should last about three seconds
choice_d: Apply the brakes fully; hold for ten seconds
explanation: When your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your safe speed, release the brakes; this application should last about three seconds.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.6, Proper Braking Technique

question: If the low air pressure warning comes on, what should you do?
choice_a: Increase speed to reach your destination faster
choice_b: Ignore it unless the buzzer also sounds
choice_c: Stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible; there might be an air leak in the system
choice_d: Switch to the trailer hand valve for all future stops
explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible, since there might be an air leak in the system.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.7, Low Air Pressure

question: When should you avoid using the parking brakes?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle is loaded
choice_b: If the brakes are very hot from a steep grade, or very wet in freezing temperatures
choice_c: Whenever the vehicle is parked on level ground
choice_d: Whenever the vehicle has ABS
explanation: Don't use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot from just having come down a steep grade, or if the brakes are very wet in freezing temperatures, since they could be damaged or freeze.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.8, Parking Brakes

question: What could happen if you leave your vehicle unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels?
choice_a: The ABS system will engage automatically
choice_b: The air compressor will automatically shut down
choice_c: Nothing, as long as the transmission is in gear
choice_d: Your vehicle might roll away and cause injury and damage
explanation: Never leave your vehicle unattended without applying the parking brakes or chocking the wheels; your vehicle might roll away and cause injury and damage.
source_note: Indiana Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, cover-dated September 9, 2022), Indiana BMV/AAMVA -- Subsection 5.4.8, Parking Brakes
